title: ZFC set theory
summary: ZFC is a major foundational theory whose objects are sets governed by explicit axiom schemes and axioms.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared classical first-order set theory context is fixed.

content.plain: ZFC is a major foundational theory whose objects are sets governed by explicit axiom schemes and axioms.
content.exact: A ZFC presentation includes extensionality, empty set, pairing, union, power set, infinity, separation and replacement schemes, foundation, and choice in first-order logic with ∈.
content.example: Natural numbers, functions, spaces, and algebraic structures can be encoded as sets inside ZFC.
content.caveat: ZFC is powerful and standard, but QEVA does not declare it the only legitimate foundation.
